function: Learned radar-sensing receiver for OFDM ISAC: suppresses Doppler-induced ICI and detects target range and velocity (DCFNet, p. 7-8). Transceiver beamforming is classical optimization, not learned (p. 5-7).
system: BS with uniform linear array, 20 transmit and 20 receive antennas, four single-antenna users, OFDM at 60 GHz with 50 MHz bandwidth; no RIS (p. 3, 10).
method: Supervised U-shaped CNN with detection head after a bank of Doppler correction filters, trained with focal loss; optional GLRT local refinement (DCFNet-LR) (p. 7-9).
data_channel: Own simulator of OFDM radar echoes from LOS far-field targets; user channel based on 3GPP TR 38.901; training dataset size not described (p. 3, 9, 10).
test_conditions: Training conditions not stated; tests use two targets in one Doppler bin, strong target 20 dB, weak-target SNR swept from -20 to 10 dB (p. 12).
baselines: Non-learned only: FFT with CFAR (ICI-contaminated, ICI-free, ICI-robust receive beamformer), 1D/2D ESPRIT, ML/GLRT search; transmit beamforming: SDR, sensing-only, communication-only; no learned baseline (p. 10-12).
metrics: Detection probability versus false-alarm probability (ROC), range and velocity RMSE, execution time, sum-rate versus beampattern gain (p. 10-12).
complexity: Measured computation time per number of detections (Fig. 12); DCFNet-LR about 175 times faster than full-grid ML (abstract: 143 times); no parameter or FLOP count (p. 1, 12).
q1_support: p. 10: "The channel from the BS to each user is modeled based on 3GPP TR 38.901" - this is the user channel of the non-learned beamformer only; DCFNet trains on own simulated LOS radar echoes (p. 3, 9), and no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data is stated for it.
q2_support: p. 12: "The stronger target signal is received at SNR = 20 dB" while the weak-target SNR is swept; this is an SNR sweep, and no test on a scenario, array or dataset unseen in training is reported (training data not described, p. 9).
q3_support: p. 12: "we evaluate the range and velocity RMSEs (root mean squared errors) of DCFNet, conventional ML, ESPRIT, and FFT methods" - all baselines are non-learned (FFT/CFAR, ESPRIT, ML, SDR, ICI-robust beamformer, p. 10); no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "reducing the computation time by approximately a factor of 175" for DCFNet-LR against full-grid ML; Fig. 12 plots the measured computation time of DCFNet and DCFNet-LR.
q5_support: p. 10: "All simulations are implemented on an AMD Ryzen" - the data are own simulations; no code or data link is given anywhere in the paper, including the conclusion (p. 13).
notes: Included as area 5 because the system communicates (multi-user downlink sum-rate) and the learned receiver serves the sensing function of the OFDM ISAC waveform; reviewer to confirm that learned ICI suppression and target detection counts as an area-5 function, since the beamformers are optimized, not learned. q1 is 0 because the 3GPP TR 38.901 channel (p. 10) models only the user link of the non-learned beamformer; the dataset used to train DCFNet is not described beyond p. 9. The abstract states 143x faster than ML search, whereas p. 12 states approximately a factor of 175.
